_why: RESIZED. The first attempt asked for 26,000 games at ~890 worlds/eval. Ladder session-replay costs ~9.5 CPU-s/game (measured locally: 631 games in 20 min at procs=5), so on Kaggle's 4 vCPU that is 18-29 h against an 11 h budget -- it could never finish, and optimizer_bakeoff only wrote its JSON when a METHOD completed, so a timeout would have yielded nothing. Now 12 evaluations at ~700 worlds = 9,250 games = ~8.0 h at 3.1 s/game, still under budget at 1.6x slower. Statistics still hold: paired sd $17,168 -> se $649 at 700 worlds, and the best-of-12 winner's curse is $1,447, which is 48% of the $3,000 effect (the rule is under half). Every evaluation is now appended to rl/bakeoff_runs/progress_<method>.jsonl as it happens, so even a kill leaves usable data.
